pr_title: fix(core): keep original whitespace intact when sanitizing srcset att…
pr_body:
…ribute

URLs in a `srcset` attribute can contain commas as part of an URL and the HTML
serializer would previously insert a space into such URLs next to the comma,
resulting in a broken URL. This commit adjusts the srcset sanitization logic to
keep the whitespace in the original srcset intact to avoid this issue.

Fixes #45164
pr_comments:
An alternative that we could consider is the actual removal of the `srcset` sanitization. My rough understanding is that modern browsers that Angular supports don't have attack vectors that could be exploited by un-sanitized `srcset` value.

This came up during the work on the image directive and we've decided to remove the `srcset` sanitization altogether (see: https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/485c6a71693fd2c786bb47a7f8aca1721d818a31).
Removing `srcset` sanitization should indeed not have any security implications in browsers that Angular supports.

@bjarkler thanks for the reply! Just wanted to confirm if it's safe to drop `srcset` sanitization for both `` and [`` tags](https://www.w3schools.com/tags/att_source_srcset.asp). We previously had a conversation about the `` tag specifically, but some logic at runtime triggers sanitization for any `srcset` attributes (without looking at the tag name). So I was wondering if it'd be ok to drop that logic altogether or update it to skip `srcset` sanitization for `` tags only. Thank you.
Sorry, I should have been more clear. :) Dropping the srcset sanitization logic altogether, i.e. both for `img` and `source` tags, should be safe.
Thnx so much for the update @bjarkler !

issue_context.title: URL sanitization breaks URLs containing commas in srcset
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

Hey,

We're using `[innerHTML]="content"` in angular, where content is HTML from WordPress. WordPress is using cloudinary which generates URLs like 

```
https://res.cloudinary.com/<container>/images/w_844,h_562/f_auto,q_auto/<id>/image.jpg
```

The code that sanitizes `srcset` splits on `,` and joins on `, ` which breaks the URL above.

Code reference: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/core/src/sanitization/url_sanitizer.ts#L58

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://codesandbox.io/s/sparkling-resonance-8dyt3u?file=/src/app/app.component.ts

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
If you look at the HTML output, one of the images are broken. The other one works.
```


### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI: 12.0.4
Node: 16.14.0
Package Manager: npm 6.14.13
OS: darwin arm64

Angular: 12.0.4
... animations, cli, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms
... platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic, platform-server
... router

Package                         Version
---------------------------------------------------------
@angular-devkit/architect       0.1200.4
@angular-devkit/build-angular   12.0.4
@angular-devkit/core            12.0.4
@angular-devkit/schematics      12.0.4
@angular/cdk                    12.1.0
@angular/material               12.1.0
@nguniversal/builders           12.0.2
@nguniversal/express-engine     12.0.2
@schematics/angular             12.0.4
rxjs                            6.6.7
typescript                      4.2.4
```


### Anything else?

A fix could be to join on "," instead. Though it will try to sanitize URLs which aren't URLs.
comments: If you have control over how those URLs are generated/inserted then you may be able to percent-encode the comma to `%2c`, avoiding the issue.

review_comments:
Quick question: [the `srcset` value](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLImageElement/srcset) may have the following structure:
```
http://example.com/a.jpg 1x, http://example.com/b.jpg 2x, http://example.com/c.jpg 2048w
```
Once we split by comma and remove whitespaces, we'd be calling `_sanitizeUrl` with values like "http://example.com/a.jpg 1x" (with extra "1x" condition). This logic was there before, so this is not a regression, but I'm wondering if we should fix that?

I'm also wondering if unescaped comma is a valid symbol that can be present in the `srcset` value?

Looks like the suffix may indeed break usages of `data:` urls, e.g. `data:image/jpeg;base64,aa 1x` is only considered valid when the `1x` suffix is stripped off. I'd propose to change this in a follow up PR though, as it's unrelated to the reported issue (and would need subsequent fw-security approval regardless, which I'd prefer we keep to a single change per PR).

> I'm also wondering if unescaped comma is a valid symbol that can be present in the srcset value?

I was looking into this last week and although `,` is a reserved character in URLs, it is accepted in the path of an URL (but not in the domain, for instance). The original issue report _is_ using commas in URLs which are interpreted as URL even when used in the `srcset` attribute. The exact syntax form [is specified here](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#srcset-attribute), which specifically calls out that a comma cannot be used as the start or end of the URL.

> I'd propose to change this in a follow up PR though, as it's unrelated to the reported issue (and would need subsequent fw-security approval regardless, which I'd prefer we keep to a single change per PR).

Sure, let's not block this PR.

> The exact syntax form [is specified here](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#srcset-attribute), which specifically calls out that a comma cannot be used as the start or end of the URL.

Thanks for sharing the link to the spec. For the input like this: 
```
http://example.com/a,b,c/d.jpg 1x
```
we'd call `_sanitizeUrl` with "http://example.com/a", "b", "c/d.jpg 1x" since we split by `,` (that was the case before you change too, I'm just trying to understand the logic better). I guess we'd need a more sophisticated way to parse `srcset`, so that we recognize the "http://example.com/a,b,c/d.jpg" as a URL, but not its chunk.
Oh, I see your point now. Yeah agreed this isn't great and it would probably be better to tokenize the value manually instead of splitting by commas only.
